correctness.rationale: The live-edge coupling identifies infection generations with minimum directed path lengths. A positive delay requires original duration at least 2, and vaccinated graph has at most n−1 vertices, giving Tv−T0≤n−4; the shortcut/chain construction attains equality for every n≥5 while reducing infections. For the five-person six-edge graph, complete 64-configuration enumeration independently recovers Ev−E0=−p(p^5−p^4−3p^3+p+1). Strict negativity of Q double prime on (0,1), with endpoint signs, gives exactly one probability crossing, rationally bracketed. All quantified boundaries p=0,1 and n≤4 are included. Standalone code passed full 64-case enumeration, all directed graphs through 4, constructions through 60, and 999 exact rational probability tests; finite checks supplement the proof.

originality.rationale: The precise sharp one-vertex delay bound and the homogeneous-edge probability threshold were not located in inspected primary full texts. Floyd et al. already supply the live-edge shortest-path identity and protection against increased infections, while Pulliam et al. demonstrate duration enhancement in different dynamical models. Holme treats extinction time and static-network distances but not vaccination-induced changes; Gutfraind treats final size. Direct logical comparisons are given in four checks below. The originality conclusion is best-knowledge with unindexed graph-theoretic reduction as a residual risk.
residual_risks: A general directed-graph source-eccentricity vertex-deletion bound may imply the deterministic n−4 portion even when not indexed under vaccination terminology.
Small Reed–Frost graph or exact-duration tables outside inspected sources might contain the six-edge threshold; search absence is not proof of priority.
Rock et al. broad review could not be read fully; no NOT_COVERING assertion is made for this source.

value.rationale: The operational outcome time to final infection is different from final infected count and can move in the opposite direction despite strict per-person vaccination protection. The sharp worst-case n−4 pathwise bound identifies precisely the smallest size permitting this; its attaining family shows the gain can scale with network size. On the minimal five-person witness, the exact homogeneous-transmission root gives a quantitative switch between shortening and lengthening, beyond an arbitrary graph instance. This is motivated by network timing and intervention endpoint choice, without extrapolating to general vaccine policy.
